notes: Same headline as torch-pipeline-parallelism: the v1 pool has essentially no distributed-PyTorch content (one hit across 56,307 instructions for a torch.distributed/all_reduce/tensor-parallel regex), so both new corpora beat it. CalibForge wins outright again - seven of my final ten - and it contributes the only task in the entire pool that names tensor parallelism (model-training_20260514_011125_001). But Terminal-Lego genuinely earns a final_top10 slot here, which it did not for the other tasks: its StackOverflow-derived PyTorch cluster (task_131xx) is mostly trivia, yet task_13171 (prove nn.LSTM equals a hand-rolled LSTMCell loop over the same weights, 25 tests) is a better task_form match than anything in TMax, and task_13180/13182/13160 are real weight-layout exercises. Note that these Terminal-Lego grades are among the ones where the packet and the newer global verifier file disagree sharply (packet weak, global strong); see verifier_notes. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the corpus where I could not find ten defensible candidates - it has exactly one PyTorch task and its shortlist for this TB2.1 task was shell-script and Clojure noise, so entries 6-10 are filler at overall 1. TerminalWorld is nearly as thin, one real nn.Module task (tw_718060) and then numerical-computing stand-ins. SWE-Smith's fvcore cluster is the honest domain match on that side; I promoted combine_file__htnzvb1x to rank 1 there because its bug is specifically about setting weight constants when bias is None, which lines up with this task's initialize-bias-to-zero requirement. No candidate appears in final_top10 that is FREE under either the packet grade or the newer global grade.
